name: Fertiliser supply
value: Hormuz closed to Gulf urea exports
summary: Gulf urea exports still stuck behind Hormuz; key export route closed
state: Hormuz, the route for about a third of seaborne urea, remains largely closed, with Argus counting at least 21 vessels holding 919,000 tonnes of urea in the Gulf on 28 Oct. IFPRI notes markets are adjusting through other suppliers, and Middle East urea was well below its April peak. A key export route closed meets the Alert line.
for_you: Higher fertiliser costs tend to feed into food prices over following seasons.

sources.title: Discovery Alert — Urea shipments: Hormuz backlog
IFPRI — How are fertilizer markets coping with the continued closure of Hormuz?

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
